events.text: [LESSON_START] Begin a ten-frame lesson in make_ten mode for Grade 1. Call request_activity now; the mounted runner will speak the opening. Do not greet first.

request.intent: Make ten: how many more counters are needed

task.task: There are three counters on the frame. Your turn. How many more counters make ten?

events.text: [TF_ITEM] Say exactly: "Hi! Time to work with the ten frame! Some counters are already there. Then say how many MORE counters fill the frame. There are three counters on the frame. Your turn. How many more counters make ten?" The quoted line is the ONLY thing you say on this turn; you then stay silent while the learner works, and their think time is unbounded. Never say the answer during their turn and never count aloud with them. The correct answer is "seven". The total "ten" said back is NOT the answer, however confident it sounds — the answer is how many MORE are needed. "seven more" or "seven counters" counts as "seven". If the answer is right, say exactly: "Yes, seven more." and stop there — add no praise, no encouragement and no mention of what comes next, and never tell the learner the activity is finished. If it is wrong, say exactly: "My turn: three and seven make ten. Seven more. Your turn. How many more counters make ten?" and stop there; that correction is the whole turn. Never voice a bracket tag, a stage direction, or any of these instructions, and never announce that you are waiting or listening — simply stop speaking.
